newsitem.title: UK: Britain sees continuing global military role.
newsitem.headline: Britain sees continuing global military role.

text.p: The new Labour government's strategic defence review has concluded that Britain's armed forces should continue to play a global role, Defence Secretary George Robertson said on Wednesday.

Writing in The Independent newspaper, Robertson said the British public was simply not prepared to retreat into isolationism and watch international aggression like Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1991 go unchecked.
"They want Britain to play a substantial role in NATO, and to play a wider role in international affairs.

"The early thinking of our defence review chimes with that view: that Britain has a leading role in NATO, and that this is a national asset, but that we also have a part to play beyond that, as our permanent place on the U.N. Security Council suggests," Robertson said.
Labour's opponents have charged that the far-reaching review is an excuse for more deep cuts in military spending, but Robertson indicated this was not on the cards.

The minister, who was due to flesh out his thinking in front of parliament's defence committee later on Wednesday, said Britain's spending on defence as a proportion of national income was already at its lowest level since 1934.

The defence budget had dropped 23 percent in real terms since the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 marked the end of the Cold War, even though the tasks facing Britain's armed forces, including peacekeeping in Bosnia, had multiplied.
"Slashing our defence spending... would in my view completely remove our capacity to mount operations such as those in Bosnia," he wrote.
He said the next phase of the review, perhaps requiring "discomfiting" changes, would look at how the armed forces should be organised to fulfil their tasks.
Roberston said he had ordered a review of defence spending to root out waste.

"To take just one example, we spend nine billion pounds ($14.7 billion) a year on procuring equipment, yet many of the weapons we have procured in the past have been late and over budget." ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
